_about: Cycles per loop iteration measured on a Ryzen 7 7735U (Zen 3+), user-mode cycles, pinned to cpu 2, L1-resident data, the slope between two buffer sizes (removes the per-call overhead). Loops compiled by gcc 16.2 -O3 -march=native. 'dogfood1': wuica 0.1.4 dogfood (aethia /data/projects/wuica-dogfood: kernels.c, bench.c, logs/), 'dogfood2': wuica 0.1.5 GUI dogfood (aethia /data/projects/wuica-gui-dogfood: kern.c, var.c, bench2.c, logs/meas5.txt). The loops are the exact blocks given to wuica; in scan_a and scan_b the exit branch to .Lout was redirected to the loop start, as in the dogfood. Notes give the data or the counter readings that matter.

dot_a.note: plain C dot product: vmulps + 8 serial vaddss

scan_c.note: memchr AVX2, 128 B, one pointer + vpmovmskb

hist_a.note: byte histogram, one table, random bytes (text: 1.21, constant: 1.15)

psum_2.note: prefix sum, 2 elements per chain step

psum_v.note: AVX2 scan, gcc's carry order (vpermd on the chain)

psum_v2.note: AVX2 scan, carry chain of one vpaddd

fir8.note: 8-tap FIR, 8 unaligned ymm loads + 8 FMA; ls_misal_loads.ma64: 3.7 per iteration

fir8_s.note: 2 aligned loads + vperm2i128 + 3 vpalignr, 3 unaligned loads; 1.5 split loads per iteration

fir8_s2.note: all window offsets by shuffles, no split loads
